Expected benefits
Time
Costs
8.w: The reasons heading explains why the project is needed and how it supports the organization's business objectives: here the end of the Leeds lease and the approved cloud strategy (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.1: These are the drivers for the project, not measurable improvements it will produce.
n.2: No project duration or benefits period is described; the lease ending is a reason for the project.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given.

8.q: Matching set (business case). Mairi Campbell is preparing the full business case for Project Skyline. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The project will run for about 19 months from the start of initiation, and the running cost savings will be realized from year three onwards.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
8.w: The time heading records the period over which the project runs and the period over which its benefits are expected to be realized (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: These are timings, not the reasons why the project is needed.
n.1: Expected benefits states the measurable improvements themselves; when the project runs and when benefits arrive is recorded under time.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given; this is about duration and timing.

8.q: Matching set (business case). Mairi Campbell is preparing the full business case for Project Skyline. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Once all applications are live, the cloud subscription and the vendor's hosted core banking service will cost about £2.1 million a year, paid from the IT operations budget.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
8.w: The costs heading covers the project's costs and the ongoing operating and maintenance costs of its products, together with how they will be funded (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: A running cost is not a reason for undertaking the project.
n.1: The charge is a cost of the investment, not an improvement it delivers, even though it is lower than today's running costs.
n.2: The yearly charge is a running cost; the time heading records how long the project runs and over what period benefits are realized.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Mairi Campbell prepares the outline business case with three options: do nothing differently, which would leave the Leeds systems with nowhere to run when the lease ends; move the Leeds systems to Falkirk and replace the old hardware; and move both sites to the cloud, as the strategy proposes. Each option is compared with the first. Is this an appropriate application of the business case technique, and why?
o: Yes, because the outline business case has to recommend the cheapest of the options that meets the lease deadline.
Yes, because doing nothing differently is the baseline against which the benefits of the other options are measured.
No, because an option that would leave the Leeds systems with no site to run in is not viable and should be dropped.
No, because the options should be limited to cloud providers, as the society's board has approved the cloud strategy.
8.w: When developing the business case, the basic options are do nothing differently, do the minimum and do more than the minimum. Do nothing differently is always considered first because it is the baseline for quantifying the other options; the difference between them is what the investment buys (see manual 5.3.1).

n.0: Justification is about value, weighing benefits against costs and risks; the cheapest option is not necessarily the best value.
n.2: Even when doing nothing differently is not viable, it is still the baseline against which the costs and benefits of the other options are measured, so it is not dropped.
n.3: Even where the direction is set, the chosen option must be justified as the best value against the alternatives.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell drafts the benefits management approach. It sets out how the £1.4 million running cost saving and the four-hour recovery time will be measured, schedules reviews in years two and three after closure, and names Mairi as the person who will measure and report these benefits after the project has closed. Is this an effective way to apply the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager prepares the benefits management approach on behalf of the executive.
Yes, because carrying out post-project benefits reviews is one of the activities in closing a project.
No, because benefits should be measured at each stage boundary rather than after the project has closed.
No, because the senior user is responsible for showing that benefits are on track, including after closure.
8.w: The senior user is responsible for specifying benefits, for demonstrating that forecast benefits are on track and for the continued realization of benefits after the project closes (see manual 6.2.4.2); post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the business, not by the project (see manual 5.3.1, 'confirm'). Mairi's project manager role ends at closure, so she cannot own the later measurement.

n.0: It is true that the project manager prepares the approach, but that does not make her the right person to measure benefits after her role has ended.
n.1: Closing a project plans the post-project benefits reviews; carrying them out is done by the business after closure.
n.2: Benefits are checked at stage boundaries, but the main savings arrive from year three, after closure, so post-project reviews are still needed.

8.q: Matching set (organizing). The project board for Project Skyline is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual is the most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive.
o: Fraser McIntyre
Aileen Docherty
Joanne Pettigrew
Lena Fischer
8.w: The executive is the single point of accountability who owns the business case and secures funding. Fraser McIntyre received the mandate, holds the IT and operations budget and sits on the executive committee (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.1: Aileen Docherty reports to Fraser McIntyre and is not the budget holder; she also wants to widen the scope, which makes her a poor choice to own the business case.
n.2: Joanne Pettigrew's teams use the applications, which suits the user interest rather than accountability for the investment.
n.3: Lena Fischer works for the supplier; the executive represents the business interest of Brennan Mutual.

8.q: Matching set (organizing). The project board for Project Skyline is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual is the most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior user.
o: Fraser McIntyre
Aileen Docherty
Joanne Pettigrew
Lena Fischer
8.w: The senior user represents those who will use the products, specifies user requirements and benefits and commits user resources. Joanne Pettigrew runs the branches and contact centre, whose teams use most of the applications being migrated (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.0: Fraser McIntyre holds the budget and the mandate, which suits the executive role.
n.1: Aileen Docherty leads the IT function, which provides services rather than using the member-facing applications.
n.3: Lena Fischer represents Stratoshift, a supplier, not the people who will use the migrated applications.

8.q: Matching set (organizing). The project board for Project Skyline is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual is the most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Senior supplier representing the cloud partner.
o: Fraser McIntyre
Aileen Docherty
Joanne Pettigrew
Lena Fischer
8.w: The senior supplier commits supplier people and resources and is accountable for the quality of the products the supplier delivers. Lena Fischer is Stratoshift's engagement director, who commits its people and is accountable for the quality of its work (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.0: Fraser McIntyre represents the business interest as executive, not the cloud partner.
n.1: Aileen Docherty is the society's own chief information officer; she cannot commit Stratoshift's people or answer for the quality of its work.
n.2: Joanne Pettigrew represents the users of the applications, not the supplier.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Using the work breakdown structure, Mairi Campbell and Nicola Graham decide that Stratoshift will deliver the landing zone and the application migrations, the core banking vendor will move its own system, and the society's IT operations team will carry out decommissioning. They record this in the commercial management approach and plan the team structure around it. Which step of the organizational design and development technique is being applied, and why?
o: Understand the organizational ecosystem, because it identifies the society's existing structures and governance.
Design the project ecosystem, because it decides how work and people are organized, using the WBS and delivery model.
Develop the project ecosystem, because it builds the skills and relationships of the people joining the project.
Manage ongoing changes to the project ecosystem, because suppliers will join and leave as the stages progress.
8.w: Designing the project ecosystem decides how the work and people will be organized; it is shaped by the work breakdown structure and the commercial management approach, including the delivery model that shows which parts external suppliers deliver (see manual 6.3.1).

n.0: Understanding the organizational ecosystem looks at the existing structures, governance and policies; here the team is deciding who will deliver which parts of the work.
n.2: Developing the ecosystem covers onboarding, skills assessment and culture once people join; the allocation of work comes first.
n.3: Managing ongoing changes deals with changing needs over the lifecycle; this is the initial design of who does what.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. To save money, Mairi Campbell proposes that the project support officer from the change team, who maintains the project's registers, also carries out business assurance for each migration wave and reports the findings to Fraser McIntyre. Victoria Sharma has asked for independent assurance of every wave. Is this an effective way to apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project board decides how project assurance is carried out and who carries it out.
Yes, because the project support officer already holds the data that business assurance needs to review.
No, because project assurance must be independent of the project manager and kept separate from project support.
No, because project assurance for a regulated firm should be carried out by internal audit rather than by staff.
8.w: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and must be independent of the project manager; it cannot be given to the project manager, team members or project support, and support must be kept separate from assurance (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). A support officer working for Mairi cannot give the independent assurance required.

n.0: The board does decide how assurance is done, but within the rule that assurance cannot be assigned to project support.
n.1: Access to the data does not provide independence; the person maintaining the registers would be checking their own work.
n.3: Assurance can be carried out by board members, people appointed from the business or external parties; it does not have to be internal audit.

8.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Project Skyline? Statement 1 of 3: Set the cost tolerance of plus or minus 7.5% for the project and document it in the project mandate.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
8.w: The business layer provides the planning standards and sets the project tolerances, documenting them in the project mandate (see manual chapter 7, table 7.1).

n.1: The executive defines tolerances for each stage; project-level tolerances are set by the business layer above the board.
n.2: The project manager sets work package tolerances and works within stage tolerances; project tolerances come from the business layer.
n.3: The team manager works within work package tolerances and has no part in setting project tolerances.

8.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Project Skyline? Statement 2 of 3: Prepare the schedule for the wave 2 migration work package.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
8.w: The team manager prepares the schedule for each work package, and a team plan where needed (see manual chapter 7, table 7.1). On Project Skyline this would be Arjun Menon for the Stratoshift migration work.

n.0: The business layer sets standards and project tolerances; it does not schedule work packages.
n.1: The executive sets stage tolerances and approves stage plans, not the schedules for individual work packages.
n.2: The project manager prepares the stage plan and work package descriptions; the detailed schedule for a work package is the team manager's.

8.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Project Skyline? Statement 3 of 3: Define the time and cost tolerances for the wave migration stage and approve its stage plan.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
8.w: The executive defines the tolerances for each stage and approves the stage plans (see manual chapter 7, table 7.1).

n.0: The business layer sets project tolerances; stage tolerances are set on the project board side by the executive.
n.2: The project manager prepares the stage plan but cannot approve it or set the tolerances that limit his or her own authority.
n.3: The team manager works within work package tolerances and does not approve stage plans.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell and Steven Clarke create a product breakdown structure for the project plan and then draw a product flow diagram. It shows that wave 2 needs the shared network product from wave 1, and that the core banking move depends on the vendor's hosted service, which the vendor will provide under its own contract. Is this an appropriate application of the plans technique, and why?
o: Yes, because the product flow diagram shows the sequence of products and their dependencies, including external ones.
Yes, because a product flow diagram replaces the need to prepare a schedule for the project plan.
No, because products supplied under a separate contract are outside the project's control and should be left out.
No, because product breakdown structures are prepared for stage plans rather than for the project plan.
8.w: In product-based planning the product breakdown structure is followed by a product flow diagram showing the sequence in which products are produced and the dependencies between them, including external products the project relies on (see manual 7.3.1).

n.1: The product flow diagram feeds the later planning steps; preparing the schedule is still a separate step of the technique.
n.2: External products are shown precisely because the project depends on them; this makes the external dependency visible and manageable.
n.3: Products are defined and analysed for every level of plan, including the project plan.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell prepares a day-by-day plan for every application in all three migration waves, covering the next 14 months, and tells the board that no further stage plans will be needed. The pilot wave, which will show how long migrations really take, has not yet run. Is this an effective way to apply the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because a detailed plan made now lets the board set the tolerances for every later stage at once.
Yes, because a linear-sequential approach needs every product and task to be planned in detail before work starts.
No, because the stage plan for the wave migration stage should be prepared by Arjun Menon as team manager.
No, because each stage plan should be prepared near the end of the previous stage, within the planning horizon.
8.w: Only the near future can be planned in detail, so PRINCE2 uses a high-level project plan plus a detailed stage plan for the current stage; each later stage plan is prepared near the end of the stage before it, when results such as the pilot wave are known (see manual 7.2.1 and 7.2.2.2).

n.0: Stage tolerances are set when each stage plan is approved; setting them all now on untested estimates weakens control.
n.1: Linear-sequential delivery defines products in detail early, but stage plans are still prepared near the end of the previous stage.
n.2: Stage plans are prepared by the project manager; team managers prepare team plans and work package schedules.

8.q: Matching set (quality). Mairi Campbell and Steven Clarke are writing the product description for a 'migrated application', to be used for every wave. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Allows a member or staff application to run in the cloud landing zone so that the society can close its data centres.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
8.w: The purpose heading explains what the product is for and why it is needed (product description composition, manual chapter 8). Here it lets each application run in the cloud so that the data centres can close.

n.1: Composition lists the parts that make up the product, not why the product is needed.
n.2: Derivation states what the product is developed from, not what it is for.
n.3: Quality specifications set out measurable characteristics the product must meet; this statement explains why the product exists.

8.q: Matching set (quality). Mairi Campbell and Steven Clarke are writing the product description for a 'migrated application', to be used for every wave. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The application running in the landing zone, its operating procedures for the new environment and its rollback procedure.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
8.w: Composition lists the parts that make up the product (product description composition, manual chapter 8): the running application, its operating procedures and its rollback procedure.

n.0: The statement lists the product's parts; it does not explain what the product is for.
n.2: Derivation identifies what the product comes from, such as the existing application; these are the parts of the finished product.
n.3: Quality specifications would state the measures each part must meet, such as passing resilience tests; this statement lists the parts.

8.q: Matching set (quality). Mairi Campbell and Steven Clarke are writing the product description for a 'migrated application', to be used for every wave. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: The existing application and its configuration in the Falkirk or Leeds data centre, and the target cloud architecture designed by Steven Clarke.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
8.w: Derivation states where the product comes from, that is the source products it is developed from (product description composition, manual chapter 8): the existing application and its configuration, plus the target architecture.

n.0: The statement describes source material, not why the product is needed.
n.1: These are inputs to the product rather than the parts of the finished migrated application.
n.3: No measurable quality criteria are stated; these are the products it is derived from.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Callum Reid's internal audit team, which reports to the audit committee and not to the project, reviews whether the project's testing of migrated applications meets the standards in the society's quality management system. Which element of quality management is this, and why?
o: Project assurance, because it gives the project board confidence that the project is being run correctly.
Quality assurance, because it is carried out independently of the project management team by a business function.
Quality control, because it checks whether the migrated applications meet their quality specifications.
Quality planning, because it confirms the standards that the quality management approach should refer to.
8.w: Quality assurance is a planned, systematic activity, carried out independently of the project management team, typically by a business function, that checks the project's quality control arrangements are appropriate (see manual 8.2.3). Internal audit reports to the audit committee, not to the project board.

n.0: Project assurance is the project board's responsibility, independent of the project manager but part of the project; internal audit here works for the audit committee, outside the project.
n.2: Quality control tests the products themselves; internal audit is reviewing whether the testing arrangements are adequate.
n.3: Quality planning produces the quality management approach and product descriptions; this review takes place during delivery.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. The product description for a migrated application requires a tested rollback for every application before switch-over. To keep wave 2 on schedule, Arjun Menon suggests testing the rollback for one application of each type and assuming that the rest will work. Mairi Campbell agrees without consulting anyone else. How well does this apply the quality practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the team manager decides which quality methods are used for the products in a work package.
It applies it well, because testing one application of each type gives the board enough confidence in the wave.
It applies it poorly, because each product should be checked against its quality specifications, and changing them needs approval.
It applies it poorly, because rollback testing should be carried out by internal audit as the quality assurance function.
8.w: Quality control checks each product against the quality specifications in its product description, and results are recorded in the quality register. The product description is part of the baseline, so relaxing a specification is a change that goes through issue and change control, not an informal agreement (see manual 8.2.2; change control is part of the issues practice, ch 10).

n.0: Quality methods are set in the product descriptions and the quality management approach; a team manager cannot drop a required test.
n.1: The specification requires a tested rollback for every application, reflecting the board's very low appetite for outages; sampling does not meet it.
n.3: Testing products is quality control by the project; internal audit provides quality assurance by reviewing whether those controls are adequate.

8.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Could arise from month 12 of the project, when wave 3 is due to finish just before the freeze begins.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
8.w: Proximity records how close in time the risk might occur (risk register composition, manual 9.2.2 and chapter 9 management products): here from month 12, just before the freeze.

n.0: The risk description sets out the cause, event and effect; timing information goes under proximity.
n.2: Impact is the estimated effect on objectives if the risk occurs, not when it might occur.
n.3: The risk response describes the actions chosen to deal with the risk, not its timing.

8.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Estimated at a five-week delay to the end of the wave migration stage and about £180,000 of extra Stratoshift day rates.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
8.w: Impact is the estimated effect on objectives if the risk occurs, expressed in the units of those objectives, such as weeks and pounds (see manual 9.2.2 and chapter 9 management products).

n.0: The description names the cause, event and effect in words; the estimated size of the effect is recorded as impact.
n.1: Proximity records when the risk might occur, not its size.
n.3: These figures estimate the consequence; they are not actions taken in response.

8.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Reduce: book the wave 3 switch-over weekends now and agree a standby weekend team with Stratoshift.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
8.w: The risk response records the chosen response type and the actions to carry it out (see manual 9.2.3.1 and chapter 9 management products). Booking slots now and arranging a standby team is a reduce response.

n.0: The description explains what might happen and why; the actions agreed to deal with it are the risk response.
n.1: Proximity records when the risk might occur, not what will be done about it.
n.2: Impact estimates the consequences; the planned actions are recorded under the response.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Steven Clarke finds that 20 of the finance applications could be moved onto the cloud provider's managed database service instead of being copied as they are. This would raise the chance that running cost savings exceed the £1.4 million forecast, although the extra saving is not certain. Mairi Campbell agrees to the redesign. Which risk response is being used, and why?
o: Exploit, because the redesign is intended to capture the extra saving for the society.
Share, because the extra saving will be divided between the society and the cloud provider.
Enhance, because action is taken now to increase the probability and impact of an opportunity.
Accept, because the opportunity is being taken without changing any of the agreed plans.
8.w: Enhance takes proactive action to increase the probability and/or impact of an opportunity; exploit would make the opportunity certain (see manual 9.2.3.1, table 9.1). The redesign makes greater savings more likely, but they remain uncertain.

n.0: Exploit removes the uncertainty so that the opportunity is certain to occur; here the extra saving is still uncertain.
n.1: Share is a pain and gain sharing arrangement with a partner; nothing in the scenario divides the saving with the provider.
n.3: Accept means taking no action now; redesigning 20 applications is a definite action.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. To avoid weekend premium rates, Arjun Menon proposes moving the online banking application on a Tuesday evening. Fraser McIntyre agrees, saying that the ten pilot applications all moved without trouble, so the risk of an outage is low. The pilot applications were chosen because they were low risk and not member-facing. How well does this apply the risk practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the board's moderate appetite for cost risk supports saving on premium rates.
It applies it well, because data from the pilot wave is being used to assess the probability of an outage on this move.
It applies it poorly, because the outage risk should be transferred to Stratoshift under the framework contract.
It applies it poorly, because it conflicts with the very low appetite for outages and rests on optimism from the pilot.
8.w: Risk decisions should respect the risk appetite and the tolerances set from it, and should guard against decision bias such as optimism bias, which assumes success and discounts unfavourable risks (see manual 9.2.1 and 9.2.4). The pilot gives little evidence about a member-facing system, and the board has a very low appetite for outages.

n.0: The moderate appetite for cost risk does not outweigh the very low appetite for outages to member-facing services.
n.1: Data should inform risk assessment, but data from low-risk, non-member-facing applications is not good evidence for online banking.
n.2: Transferring financial impact does not remove the outage to members, which is what the board has a very low appetite for.

8.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 1 of 3: Update the issue register with the status of Aileen Docherty's request to add a data platform.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
8.w: Project support administers the issue and change control procedures by maintaining the issue register (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.0: The senior user makes decisions on escalated issues; keeping the register up to date is an administrative task.
n.1: The project manager manages the procedure and keeps the register only where there is no project support; here a support officer is provided.
n.2: The team manager implements corrective actions in the work package; the issue register is maintained for the whole project.

8.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 2 of 3: Write new product descriptions and a new work package for the extra monitoring dashboards that the board has approved.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
8.w: The project manager implements corrective actions, for example creating new product descriptions and work packages when extra scope has been agreed (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.0: The senior user decides on escalated issues; planning the approved change is the project manager's work.
n.2: The team manager implements corrective actions within a work package once it has been authorized; creating new work packages is the project manager's job.
n.3: Project support maintains the register; it does not write product descriptions or authorize work.

8.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 3 of 3: Decide on an escalated request to move the branch systems a month earlier, focusing on protecting the benefits expected for member services.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
8.w: The senior user makes decisions on escalated issues with a focus on safeguarding the expected benefits (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.1: The issue has been escalated beyond the project manager's authority, so the decision sits with the board.
n.2: The team manager does not decide escalated issues; it implements corrective actions in its work package.
n.3: Project support records the decision in the register but does not make it.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. During testing, the mortgage servicing application recovers from a simulated failure in six hours. Its product description requires recovery within four hours. Arjun Menon tells Mairi Campbell that a fix would delay wave 2 by three weeks. Which type of issue is this, and why?
o: A request for change, because the four-hour recovery requirement may now need to be relaxed to six hours.
An off-specification, because the product will not meet a quality specification set in its product description.
A risk rather than an issue, because the application has not yet been switched over to the cloud.
A business opportunity, because six hours is still a large improvement on the current 24 hours.
8.w: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications (issue types, manual chapter 10). The product description requires recovery within four hours and testing shows six, so the application is off-specification; the board or change authority may later grant a concession or require a fix.

n.0: A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; relaxing the requirement might be one response, but the issue raised is that the product fails its specification.
n.2: The shortfall has already been found in testing, so it is an issue, not an uncertain future event.
n.3: A business opportunity is an unexpected positive consequence; failing the required recovery time is a defect against the specification.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage, which is forecast to stay within its tolerances. Aileen Docherty asks for a new data platform to be added to the project. Mairi Campbell records the request in the issue register and assesses its impact on cost, the lease deadline, the risks and the business case. It would cost £900,000, well beyond the change budget delegated to her, so she sends an issue report with options and a recommendation to the project board. How well does this apply the issues practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the request is captured, assessed and recommended, then referred to those with authority to decide.
It applies it well, because the project manager is the change authority for every request for change on the project.
It applies it poorly, because a request for change should stay in the daily log until the board says it is a formal issue.
It applies it poorly, because a request for change of this size should be escalated to the board in an exception report.
8.w: The issue technique is capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement; a request beyond the project manager's delegated authority is referred, with options and a recommendation, to whoever holds that authority, ultimately the project board (see manual 10.3.1 and 10.2.4). An issue report is the right vehicle when the stage is within tolerance.

n.1: The board is the ultimate authority and may delegate some authority, but here the cost is far beyond what was delegated to Mairi.
n.2: A request for change that needs a formal decision is a formal issue and belongs in the issue register; the daily log is for informal issues.
n.3: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance; the stage is within tolerance, so an issue report is used.

8.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 1 of 3: Arjun Menon tells Mairi Campbell, at the frequency set in the work package, how far the wave 2 migrations have progressed and what risks his team has found.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
8.w: A checkpoint report is produced by the team manager for the project manager on the status of a work package, at the frequency defined in the work package description (see manual chapter 11, progress management products).

n.1: Highlight reports go from the project manager to the board on the status of the stage.
n.2: Exception reports go from the project manager to the board when stage or project tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.
n.3: The lessons log records lessons, not regular work package status.

8.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: Mairi Campbell informs the board that wave 3 is now forecast to end five weeks late, beyond the stage's time tolerance, and sets out the options and her recommendation.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
8.w: An exception report is produced by the project manager when a stage plan or project plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances; it sets out the consequences, options and a recommendation (see manual chapter 11 and 11.3.1).

n.0: Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the project manager on a work package.
n.1: Highlight reports give routine stage status; a forecast breach of stage tolerance needs an exception report.
n.3: The lessons log records lessons; it is not used to escalate a forecast breach.

8.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: The list of application dependencies at the Leeds site proved incomplete, so discovery work for future waves should start at least six weeks earlier.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
8.w: The lessons log is the informal repository for lessons that apply to this or future projects; lessons are recorded as they arise and acted on throughout (see manual chapter 11 and 2.2).

n.0: A checkpoint report gives work package status; a lesson for future waves is recorded in the lessons log.
n.1: A highlight report may mention lessons, but the lesson itself is recorded in the lessons log.
n.2: Nothing is forecast to exceed tolerance; this is a lesson, not an exception.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. The stage plan sets a time tolerance of two weeks for each migration wave. Arjun Menon's checkpoint report forecasts that wave 3 will finish five weeks late because the core banking vendor has delayed a shared interface. Mairi Campbell cannot find a way to recover the time within tolerance. What should Mairi do NEXT?
o: Prepare an exception plan for the rest of the stage and submit it to the board for approval.
Take corrective action by moving applications between waves and report it in the next highlight report.
Raise an exception report to the project board, setting out the options and her recommendation.
Ask the business layer to increase the project's time tolerance so that wave 3 can finish later.
8.w: When stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, the project manager escalates by raising an exception report to the project board with options and a recommendation; the board then decides, for example by asking for an exception plan (see manual 11.2.6 and 11.3.1).

n.0: An exception plan is prepared after the board has considered the exception report and asked for one; it is not the first step.
n.1: Corrective action is for deviations that can be dealt with within tolerance; Mairi cannot recover the time.
n.3: Stage tolerance breaches go to the project board; the business layer deals with breaches of project tolerance.

8.q: Project Skyline is at the start of the foundations stage. Stratoshift's Pune team has not worked with the society's systems before. Mairi Campbell agrees in the work package that Arjun Menon will send checkpoint reports daily during switch-over weekends and twice a week at other times, moving to weekly once the pilot wave is complete. Is this an effective way to apply the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because reporting is more frequent while the team is new and the work riskier, and eases as confidence grows.
Yes, because time-driven checkpoint reports remove the need for event-driven controls during the stage.
No, because the frequency of checkpoint reports is set by the project board in the PID and should not vary.
No, because checkpoint reports during switch-over weekends should go directly to the project board.
8.w: Reporting frequency should reflect the level of control needed: an inexperienced team, or risky work, warrants more frequent reporting until confidence grows (see manual 11.2.4). Checkpoint frequency is agreed in the work package between the project manager and team manager.

n.1: Time-driven and event-driven controls are both needed; regular reports do not replace stage-end decisions or exception reports.
n.2: Checkpoint frequency is agreed in each work package description and can differ between work packages and over time.
n.3: Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the project manager; the board receives highlight reports from the project manager.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell has been spending a day every fortnight combining spreadsheets from Edinburgh, Pune and Falkirk to produce her highlight report. She arranges for the migration tool's data to feed a shared dashboard automatically, from which Arjun Menon's checkpoint reports and her highlight reports are produced in the format the board prefers. Is this an appropriate application of the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the dashboard can set the work package tolerances from the data it collects on each migration.
Yes, because data and automation remove manual consolidation and present progress in the form stakeholders prefer.
No, because highlight reports should be compiled by hand by the project manager so that she can check the figures.
No, because a shared dashboard cannot be used once the audit committee has asked for a monthly written update.
8.w: The progress practice encourages using data and systems to track progress and support decisions: automation removes the manual consolidation of separate sources, and information can be presented in the format stakeholders prefer (see manual 11.2.7).

n.0: Data supports tracking and forecasting, but tolerances are set by the management levels, not by tools.
n.2: Manual compilation is not required; automating the consolidation makes reporting faster and more consistent, and the project manager still reviews the report.
n.3: The written update to the audit committee can still be produced from the same data; the dashboard does not prevent it.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Mairi Campbell works with Steven Clarke and Nicola Graham to compare moving applications unchanged with redesigning them for the cloud, and in-house delivery with using a partner. Drawing on the lesson from the society's earlier fixed-scope contract dispute, they recommend using Stratoshift under its framework contract, with work agreed one package at a time, and migrating in waves. Is this an appropriate application of the 'select the project approach' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it decides how the work will be delivered, including the use of third parties and the delivery method.
Yes, because the chosen approach removes the need to compare business options in the outline business case.
No, because the project approach is agreed in initiation as one of the management approaches.
No, because choosing a supplier belongs to the commercial management approach, which is agreed after authorization.
8.w: In 'select the project approach' the project manager decides how the work will be approached, for example in-house or through third parties, build or buy, and which delivery method to use, so that initiation starts on a sound basis (see manual 13.4.5). Using lessons from the earlier dispute strengthens the choice.

n.1: The project approach is about how to deliver; the outline business case still compares the business options to justify the investment.
n.2: The project approach is selected in starting up a project and included in the project brief; the management approaches are agreed later, in initiation.
n.3: The commercial management approach is agreed in initiation, before the project is authorized, and it builds on the project approach chosen in starting up.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. The society's board has given the mandate to Fraser McIntyre, who will be the executive. Fraser now chooses Mairi Campbell from the change team as project manager and agrees her responsibilities with her. Which role is responsible for the 'appoint the executive and the project manager' activity?
o: The business layer, which commissioned the project and identified its executive.
The executive, who appoints the project manager to manage the project on his behalf.
The project board, once the senior user and senior supplier have been appointed.
The project manager, who confirms her own role description with the executive.
8.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the executive and the project manager', the business layer is accountable and the executive is responsible; the project manager then manages the project day to day on the executive's behalf (see manual 13.4.1 and table 13.2).

n.0: The business layer is accountable for the activity; the executive is responsible for carrying it out, including appointing the project manager.
n.2: The rest of the board is appointed later, in 'appoint the project management team'; it does not carry out this activity.
n.3: The project manager is the person being appointed; she is not responsible for her own appointment.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Fraser McIntyre tells Mairi Campbell that, because the society's board has already approved the cloud strategy, there is no need for a project brief or an initiation stage plan. He asks her to start initiation work with Stratoshift next week and report back in two months. Is this an effective way to carry out starting up a project, and why?
o: Yes, because approval of the strategy by the society's board acts as the authority to initiate the project.
Yes, because starting up can be shortened when a programme has supplied most of the project brief.
No, because starting up puts the prerequisites for initiation in place before an explicit decision to initiate.
No, because the business layer, rather than the executive, should carry out starting up on a project this size.
8.w: Starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiation are in place, including the project brief and the initiation stage plan, and the decision to initiate must be explicit, taken by the board in 'authorize initiation' (see manual 13.1 and 13.4.8). A strategy approval is not that decision.

n.0: A strategy sets direction for the business; the project board still has to authorize initiation explicitly on the basis of a project brief.
n.1: It is true that a programme can supply much of the brief, but Project Skyline is not part of a programme and no brief exists.
n.3: Starting up is led by the project manager, with the business layer and executive making the appointments; the business layer does not run the whole process.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell asks Joanne Pettigrew which weekend in March would least disrupt the branches and contact centre when the branch systems move. Joanne checks with her branch managers and replies the next day with a preferred weekend and the dates to avoid. Is this an appropriate application of the 'give ongoing direction' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user is accountable for approving the stage plan, which includes the switch-over dates.
Yes, because board members can give informal guidance, and the senior user gives direction on user matters.
No, because direction from the board should be given collectively at a formal meeting of the board.
No, because a request for advice has to be raised as an issue in the issue register before the board responds.
8.w: Giving ongoing direction includes informal guidance and responses to requests for advice at any time, given collectively or by individual board members; in the recommended RACI the senior user is responsible for user-related direction (see manual 14.4.3).

n.0: The executive approves stage plans; the senior user's part here is giving user-related direction.
n.2: Ongoing direction can be given informally and by individual board members, not only at formal meetings.
n.3: Requests for advice can be made informally; not every question to the board is an issue for the register.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Before each board meeting, the board's business assurance checks the figures in Mairi Campbell's highlight report against the migration tool's records and the stage plan, and tells Fraser McIntyre whether the report gives a fair picture. Which practice is being applied by the directing a project process, and why?
o: Quality, because the checks confirm that the migrated applications meet their quality specifications.
Organizing, because project assurance is a role that the project board appoints to support its work.
Risk, because checking the figures reduces the chance of an unexpected breach of tolerance.
Progress, because the board makes sure that reporting is fair by validating the highlight reports.
8.w: In directing a project the progress practice is applied by the board assuring itself that reporting is fair, validating highlight and end stage reports, and responding to exception reports (see manual chapter 14, table 14.3).

n.0: The checks are on reported progress figures, not on whether products meet their quality specifications.
n.1: Assurance is a role from the organizing practice, but the activity described is validating progress reporting.
n.2: Accurate reporting supports control, but checking reported progress is part of the progress practice, not risk management.

8.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the 'initiating a project' process. Board members are busy with the year end, so Fraser McIntyre emails Mairi Campbell telling her to start the foundations stage at once. He says the board will review the PID, the project plan and the foundations stage plan at its next meeting in six weeks. Stratoshift is ready to begin building the landing zone. Is this an effective way to carry out directing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the board can give approval without a meeting when the executive gives a documented instruction.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the project and can authorize the stage on his own.
No, because the decision to start a delivery stage belongs to the business layer rather than the board.
No, because delivery should not start until the board has approved the PID and authorized the first delivery stage.
8.w: In directing a project the board authorizes the project by approving the PID, and a stage starts when the board authorizes its stage plan; delivery should not begin before these decisions (see manual 14.4.2 and 14.4.4). Here the board has not yet reviewed any of the documents.

n.0: Decisions can be made without a formal meeting when the members agree, but here the board has not reviewed the PID or stage plan at all.
n.1: The executive is accountable, but authorizing the project and the stage are board decisions based on the PID and stage plan.
n.2: The project board authorizes each stage; the business layer sets project tolerances and decides on project-level exceptions.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell agrees with the board that it will receive highlight reports every two weeks, that each stage will end with a stage boundary review, and that each migration wave has a time tolerance of two weeks within the stage plan. She also agrees how she will control Stratoshift's work through work packages and checkpoint reports. Is this an appropriate application of the 'establish project controls' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it agrees the board's control after initiation and how the project manager will control the teams.
Yes, because once project controls are agreed, the board no longer needs to authorize each stage separately.
No, because project controls are agreed in starting up a project, before initiation is authorized.
No, because tolerances for each wave should be set by the business layer in the project mandate.
8.w: 'Establish project controls' agrees the level and mechanism of control the board will have after initiation, and how the project manager will control the work of team managers (see manual 15.4.3). Reporting frequency, stage boundaries, tolerances and work package controls are all part of this.

n.1: Project controls include the stage boundaries; the board still authorizes each stage.
n.2: Project controls are established in initiation, once the management approaches are agreed.
n.3: The business layer sets project tolerances; tolerances within a stage plan are set by the board.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell updates the outline business case with the costs and timescales from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log. Fraser McIntyre will be asked to approve it. Which role should be consulted during the 'prepare the full business case' activity?
o: The business layer, represented by the society's executive committee.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell, who is preparing the document.
Project assurance, acting on behalf of the project board.
The executive, Fraser McIntyre, who will be asked to approve it.
8.w: In the recommended RACI for 'prepare the full business case', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible, project assurance is consulted and the business layer is not involved (see manual 15.4.5).

n.0: The business layer is not involved in preparing the full business case.
n.1: The project manager is responsible for preparing it, not consulted.
n.3: The executive is accountable for the business case, not consulted.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell plans to leave the digital and data management approach until the foundations stage, saying that member data will not move until the pilot wave. The project will copy member data between the sites and the cloud, and old hardware must be disposed of with certificates confirming that member data has been destroyed. Is this an effective way to carry out initiating a project, and why?
o: Yes, because handling member data is a technical matter for Stratoshift's work package descriptions.
Yes, because the management approaches are reviewed at each stage boundary, so this one can be added at the first.
No, because data protection requirements belong in the quality management approach rather than a separate approach.
No, because how data is kept secure through the lifecycle and afterwards should be agreed before the project is authorized.
8.w: The digital and data management approach is one of the management approaches agreed in initiation and approved with the PID; it describes how data will be created, used, secured and managed through the lifecycle and afterwards (see manual 15.4.2 and chapter 11, progress management products). With member data moving and being destroyed, it is needed before authorization.

n.0: Work packages apply the approaches; the approach itself must first be agreed at project level so the board can approve it.
n.1: Approaches are reviewed and updated at stage boundaries, but they are first agreed in initiation as part of the PID.
n.2: The digital and data management approach is a separate approach in PRINCE2 7; the quality management approach covers quality standards and responsibilities.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell and Arjun Menon draft the wave 1 work package together over a video call. It lists the 35 applications and their product descriptions, time, cost and scope tolerances, weekly checkpoint reports, the constraint that no switch-over may take place on month-end processing days, and how each application will be handed to operations. Arjun confirms his team can deliver it before work starts. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because authorizing the work package allows Arjun Menon to report progress directly to the project board.
Yes, because the work package is co-created with the team manager, who confirms it can be delivered before work starts.
No, because the work package should also carry a benefits tolerance for the running cost savings.
No, because work for an external supplier should be agreed with the senior supplier rather than the team manager.
8.w: In 'authorize a work package' the project manager defines the work package, builds a relationship with the team manager, co-creates and reviews it with them, confirms that they accept it and then authorizes the start (see manual 16.4.1). The contents, including scope, cost and time tolerances, constraints and checkpoint frequency, fit a work package description.

n.0: The team manager reports to the project manager through checkpoint reports; the board receives highlight reports from the project manager.
n.2: A work package description carries scope, cost and time tolerances; benefits tolerance is not set at work package level.
n.3: The senior supplier commits Stratoshift's resources at board level, but work packages are agreed between the project manager and the team manager.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon reports that two applications in wave 2 are not ready to move. Staying within stage tolerance, Mairi Campbell swaps them with two applications from wave 3 and updates the work packages and the stage plan. Which role is accountable for the 'take corrective action' activity?
o: The executive, Fraser McIntyre.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell.
The team manager, Arjun Menon.
Project support, from the change team.
8.w: In the recommended RACI for 'take corrective action', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible for selecting and triggering the action within tolerance, and project support is informed (see manual 16.4.6 and table 16.2).

n.1: Mairi Campbell is responsible for taking the corrective action, but accountability sits with the executive.
n.2: The team manager carries out the changed work through the work packages; he is not accountable for the activity.
n.3: Project support is informed of corrective action, not accountable for it.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. The stage plan allows each migration wave a time tolerance of two weeks. Arjun Menon's checkpoint report forecasts that wave 1 will finish four days late because two engineers are ill, and Mairi Campbell expects to recover most of the time in the next fortnight. She immediately sends an exception report to the project board. Is this an effective way to carry out controlling a stage, and why?
o: Yes, because Fraser McIntyre asked to be told at once of any slip in a migration wave.
Yes, because later waves depend on earlier ones, so any delay to a wave should be escalated to the board.
No, because exception reports are raised by the team manager and passed to the board by the project manager.
No, because the slip is within tolerance, so she should act on it herself and report it in her highlight report.
8.w: The project manager escalates through an exception report when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; a forecast deviation within tolerance is handled by corrective action in controlling a stage and reported in the highlight report (see manual 16.4.6 and 11.2.6).

n.0: Fraser McIntyre asked to be told if a wave was forecast to slip by more than two weeks, which is the tolerance; four days is within it.
n.1: The dependency between waves is real, but it is reflected in the two-week tolerance; a slip within tolerance is not an exception.
n.2: The project manager raises exception reports; a team manager raises a forecast breach of work package tolerance with the project manager as an issue.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon receives the draft wave 2 work package. With his team in Pune, he finds that two planned switch-over weekends fall during a major Indian festival when most of the engineers are on leave. He agrees new dates with Mairi Campbell that avoid the society's month-end days, then accepts the work package and prepares a team plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered and that it is achievable.
Yes, because accepting the work package allows the team manager to set new tolerances for the work package.
No, because the team manager should accept the work package as issued and raise any problems later as issues.
No, because a team plan for a work package has to be approved by the project board before work starts.
8.w: In 'accept a work package' the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the constraints, reporting and procedures, and whether the work is achievable, then agrees to deliver it, producing a team plan if needed (see manual 17.4.1).

n.1: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager; the team manager agrees to deliver within them.
n.2: Accepting a work package includes checking that it is achievable and agreeing changes before accepting; known problems should be resolved first.
n.3: Team plans are optional and produced by the team manager; the project board does not approve them.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon's team is migrating the wave 2 applications, updating the quality register as each test is passed and notifying Mairi Campbell of new risks. Which role is accountable for the 'execute a work package' activity?
o: The senior supplier, Lena Fischer, who commits Stratoshift's people.
The team manager, Arjun Menon, who leads the engineers doing the work.
The executive, Fraser McIntyre, who is accountable for the whole project.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell, who authorized the work package.
8.w: In the recommended RACI for 'execute a work package', the project manager is accountable and project assurance is consulted; the business layer and executive are not involved (see manual 17.4.2 and table 17.2).

n.0: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of supplier products at board level, but the board is not involved in managing product delivery.
n.1: The team manager carries out the work package; accountability for the activity sits with the project manager.
n.2: The executive is not involved in executing a work package.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Lena Fischer, who sits on the project board as senior supplier, phones Arjun Menon and tells him to move three engineers to another Stratoshift client for two weeks, delaying part of the wave 2 work package. Arjun does so and mentions it in his next checkpoint report. Is this an effective way to carry out managing product delivery, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior supplier commits Stratoshift's people and can decide where its engineers work.
Yes, because the delay was reported to the project manager in the team manager's next checkpoint report.
No, because the team manager takes instructions on the work package from the project manager, not from a board member.
No, because instructions to a team manager should come from the executive as the single point of accountability.
8.w: In managing product delivery the team manager works to the work package agreed with the project manager, notifies the project manager of issues and takes any action required by the project manager, not instructions directly from the board (see manual 17.4.2). Lena should raise the resourcing problem with Mairi.

n.0: The senior supplier commits supplier resources at board level, but changing an authorized work package should go through the project manager.
n.1: Reporting the change afterwards does not make it acceptable; the project manager should decide before the work package is changed.
n.3: Neither the executive nor other board members instruct team managers; direction flows from the board to the project manager.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. After Mairi Campbell's exception report about wave 3 slipping into the December change freeze, the board asks for an exception plan. Mairi records the request in the project log and prepares a plan from the current position to the end of the stage, then updates the project plan and business case to reflect it. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare exception plan' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because Mairi can approve the exception plan herself while the project stays within project tolerance.
Yes, because the plan replaces the stage plan from the current position, and the effect on the project is assessed.
No, because an exception plan is prepared in controlling a stage as part of escalating issues and risks.
No, because the exception plan should replace Arjun Menon's team plan rather than the stage plan.
8.w: When the board asks for an exception plan, the project manager records the request, prepares a plan from the current position to the end of the stage to replace the stage plan, and reviews and updates the project plan and business case (see manual chapter 18, 'prepare exception plan').

n.0: The project board approves a stage-level exception plan; the project manager cannot approve her own plan.
n.2: The exception report is raised in controlling a stage; the exception plan itself is prepared in managing a stage boundary.
n.3: Exception plans replace stage or project plans; they are not produced for team plans.

8.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell reviews how the Pune engineers and Hugh Bannerman's operations staff have worked together, including fatigue after repeated switch-over weekends, and records lessons on team health and well-being for the end stage report. Which practice is being applied by the managing a stage boundary process, and why?
o: Progress, because the stage's actual costs and dates are compared with those in the stage plan.
Organizing, because team performance, health and well-being are reviewed to inform lessons and the report.
Quality, because the quality register is checked to confirm the stage's quality activities were completed.
Issues, because the fatigue of the teams should be recorded and assessed as a formal issue.
8.w: In managing a stage boundary the organizing practice is applied by reviewing the project team's performance, health and well-being, feeding lessons and the end stage report (see manual chapter 18, table 18.3).

n.0: Comparing costs and dates with the plan is not what Mairi is doing; she is reviewing how the teams worked together and their well-being.
n.2: Checking the quality register is how the quality practice is applied at a stage boundary; this review is about the people.
n.3: Nothing is said about raising an issue; the review gathers lessons on team health for the report.

8.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the foundations stage. Mairi Campbell sends the board the wave migration stage plan and the updated business case, but no end stage report. She says the fortnightly highlight reports have already told the board how the foundations stage went. Is this an effective way to carry out managing a stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because highlight reports are time-driven controls that already cover the status of the stage for the board.
Yes, because an end stage report is needed when an exception plan is being presented to the board.
No, because the end stage report should be written by project assurance for the board to review.
No, because the board needs the end stage report to review how the stage performed before deciding.
8.w: In 'evaluate the stage' the project manager prepares the end stage report, which gives the board the information it needs to review the stage just ending and decide what to do next; it is an event-driven control at the stage boundary (see manual chapter 18 and 11.2.2).

n.0: Highlight reports give periodic status during the stage; the stage-end decision is supported by the end stage report.
n.1: It is the other way round: an end stage report is always prepared at a stage end, and with an exception plan it is needed only if the board asks for one.
n.2: The project manager is responsible for the end stage report; project assurance is consulted.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the decommissioning stage and approaching closure. Mairi Campbell confirms that all products have been delivered, including certificates confirming that member data on the old hardware was destroyed. She updates the project plan with actual figures, closes the project log, archives the project records in line with the digital and data management approach and prepares closure messages for staff and suppliers. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare planned closure' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it confirms the project can close, updates the plan with actuals and secures the project's records.
Yes, because closing the project log also completes the post-project benefits reviews for the business.
No, because closure activities should be planned as a separate stage that follows decommissioning.
No, because project records should be destroyed once the products have been handed over to operations.
8.w: In 'prepare planned closure' the project manager confirms the project is ready to close, updates the project plan with actuals, closes the project log, makes sure project information is secured and archived, and prepares closure communications (see manual 19.4.1).

n.1: Post-project benefits reviews are planned during closure and carried out by the business after the project ends.
n.2: Closing a project is part of the final stage; closure is never planned as a stage of its own.
n.3: Project information is secured and archived so that it can be used later, for example in audits and benefits reviews.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the 'closing a project' process. Mairi Campbell works through the product register, confirming that each product, including every migrated application and each disposal certificate, is complete or has a follow-on action, and then closes the register. Which practice is being applied by the closing a project process, and why?
o: Quality, because the product register records whether each product passed its quality checks.
Issues, because any product that is not complete has to be raised as an off-specification.
Plans, because the product register is checked and closed to confirm the products of the plan.
Progress, because the product register is used to compare actual progress with the stage plan.
8.w: In closing a project the plans practice is applied by checking and closing the product register, which lists all the products of the plan and their status (see manual chapter 19, table 19.3).

n.0: Quality checks and their results are recorded in the quality register; the product register lists the products and their status.
n.1: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specification; an incomplete product with a follow-on action is not necessarily one.
n.3: The product register is not being used to track progress against the stage plan; it is being checked and closed.

8.q: Project Skyline is in the decommissioning stage. The £1.4 million yearly saving will not appear until year three, well after both data centres have closed. Mairi Campbell proposes keeping the project open, with herself as project manager, until the saving can be measured, so that the board can confirm the benefit before closing. Is this an effective way to carry out closing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive stays accountable for the business case until all of the benefits have been realized.
Yes, because confirming benefits is one of the steps of the business case technique in PRINCE2 7.
No, because later benefits should be measured in post-project reviews planned in the benefits management approach.
No, because benefits stop being measured once the products have been handed over to operations.
8.w: A project should have a clear end rather than drift on; benefits that arise after closure are assessed in post-project benefits reviews, which closing a project plans by updating the benefits management approach and which the business carries out (see manual 19.2, 19.3 and 5.3.1).

n.0: Whoever is accountable for the business case, the project should close once its products are accepted; later benefits are confirmed in post-project reviews, and the senior user remains responsible for their realization after closure.
n.1: Confirming benefits is a step of the technique, but it mostly happens after closure, so it does not justify keeping the project open.
n.3: Benefits continue to be measured after handover, through post-project reviews carried out by the business.
